newsitem.title: CHINA: East China port opens 120,000-dwt floating dock.
newsitem.headline: East China port opens 120,000-dwt floating dock.

text.p: A huge floating dock for renovating and repairing 120,000 deadweight-tonne ships has gone into operation in Qingdao port in China's eastern province of Shandong, the China Daily said on Tuesday.
The $24 million, 250-metre (820-ft-long) long dock at Qingdao's Beihai Shipyard could handle vessels up to 43 metres (141 ft) wide and would be China's largest such dock, the newspaper said.
The facility would allow the shipyard to repair 40 more ships and generate an additional 200 million yuan ($24 million) a year in revenue, it said.
City officials were considering building larger docks capable of handling ships of up to 400,000-dwt, it said.
Authorities would launch more dock projects in coastal cities and along major rivers to handle a forecast rise in China's share of the ship repair and shipbuilding business, it said.
The Shanhaiguan Shipyard in the northern province of Hebei was building a 150,000-dwt dry dock expected to open in two years, it said.

China's share of the world ship repair business would grow to five percent by 2000 from the current 2.5 percent while its chunk of global shipbuilding would rise to 10 percent from five percent now, it said.
